evidence: The hunk shows `seen[id]` dedupe recording `Gates: row.ID` for only the first in-scope row, and `Gates` is now user-visible; the reviewer offered 'document or test' and the agent did both in 5700430, with a test that reads its expectation from the queue order.
guidance_note: When a walk that dedupes starts carrying a per-occurrence payload, state which occurrence wins at the dedupe site and pin it with a two-row fixture in the original PR.

evidence: Round-0 hunk keeps 'exactly those six cases' while 08-claims-and-identity.md says seven; commit 4193340 changes it to 'exactly those seven cases'.
guidance_note: When adding a variant to a sealed sum, grep every doc for the old cardinality word ('six') and the sibling variant names before pushing, not just the doc you were editing.

evidence: The sentence was edited in the PR (line numbers bumped) yet kept 'the three other served outcomes announce (`:100-108`)'; 4193340 shows 'four other served outcomes announce (`:100-117`)'.
guidance_note: When re-anchoring line numbers in a sentence, re-read the sentence's counts and ranges against the new code too, since an edited sentence is one the author already owns.

evidence: `runNextRow` switched over only four served outcomes and its doc comment claimed totality; instead of adding one case the agent moved narrowing into `servedRow` and added `TestServedRowIsTotalOverTheSealedSum` over all seven variants, which closes the class rather than the instance.
guidance_note: When adding a sum variant, grep for every type switch over the sum (tests included), not only the production renderer that panics.

evidence: The hunk changes the asserted type to `ServedFromDependency` while the unchanged comment above still says it comes back as `ServedFromNewLane`; the agent updated the comment in 5700430.
guidance_note: When changing what a test asserts, re-read the test's own doc comment and name in the same edit.

evidence: The agent's F8 reply says 'the seven lines I added inside gatingDependencies shifted 24 citations', i.e. the F1 fix (5700430) moved `maxNamedPerKind` off `:604`; flagged commit 4193340 only edits 06-issue-commands.md and did not cause it. Whether 3f23da7 preceded the reviewed head is not shown (its diff is absent), though the thread is marked outdated.
guidance_note: In a repo whose docs cite file:line, re-run the citation relocation in the same commit as any code insertion made to answer a finding, not in a later pass.

evidence: The '(EpicLane, NewLane)' enumeration above `renderNextOutcome` was left incomplete by the original PR's `ServedFromDependency` case; flagged commit 4193340 is docs-only, so the flag is a false positive and this was a round-0 miss.
guidance_note: When adding a case to a switch, grep the enclosing function's doc comment for lists of the sibling case names and extend them.

evidence: `next_route.go:533` was right in the original PR (round-0 hunks cite it); the seven lines the F1 fix added inside `gatingDependencies` pushed `onPathDependency` to 540, per the agent's own reply. 3f23da7's diff is not in the packet, so whether it really preceded this round is unverified.
guidance_note: Treat any code insertion made to answer a finding as a citation-shifting change and relocate citations in that same commit.

evidence: The hunk shows the `gatedDep` comment directly abutting the `gatingDependencies` comment block, so Go attaches the whole block to `gatedDep`; `gatedDep` already existed in round 0 (F1's hunk uses it), so the flag on docs-only 4193340 is a false positive and the defect is original.
guidance_note: When inserting a declaration between a doc comment and the symbol it documents, move the new declaration above the comment or separate it with a blank line, and check with go doc.

narrative: The PR adds a seventh NextOutcome variant. Round 0 found real doc-count drift and a non-total test helper, all accepted correctly. Round 1's two citation findings came from the seven lines the F1 fix inserted, and the other two (an enumeration comment and a doc comment attached to the wrong symbol) were original misses. Round 1 would have happened anyway because of those two, so no round is attributable to fixes alone.
guidance_observations: Every finding in this PR is a stale enumeration, count, or citation left behind by adding a sum variant or inserting lines; one grep for sibling variant names and cardinality words before the first push would have cleared most of them.
The citation relocation ran in a separate commit (3f23da7) from the code insertion that shifted the citations, which left a window in which the reviewer flagged them.

evidence: The agent ran both binaries and confirmed `lit quickstart --eject all` prints byte-identical output, so the changelog example demonstrated no change. Rewording the quickstart refusal went beyond the finding, and that new message is what F18 later caught.
guidance_note: Run every concrete command a changelog cites against both the base and head binaries before the first push.

evidence: `withWorkspaceSchema` rebuilt `wsLeaf{fs, positionals, work}` without `usage`; the agent made all three adapters use `adaptLeaf` and verified `lit upgrade a b c` prints the leaf's own usage on the built binary.
guidance_note: When adding a field to a struct that adapters rebuild field by field, grep every literal construction of that struct, and test through the production wrapper rather than the inner constructor.

evidence: `leafPaths` recursed only into `Subcommands`, never testing a family's bare leaf; the agent confirmed by mutation that `rankLeaf` with `allPositionals` had stayed green, and the walk now emits 17 bare forms.
guidance_note: When a test claims 'every command', mutate one known leaf before trusting the walk, to prove the walk reaches it.

evidence: The hunk deletes the `fs.NArg()` check but keeps 'This is init's ONLY arity check' directly above it; the comment was rewritten in a1dc06b.
guidance_note: When deleting a check, delete or rewrite every comment that names it in the same hunk; grep the deleted call for adjacent comment lines.

evidence: Deleting the per-leaf `NArg` checks left `nextUsage`, `view.usage()`, and `quickstartUsage` unreferenced; the agent wired all three and measured that 37 of 66 leaves had fallen to the generic message, which justified the derived fallback.
guidance_note: When deleting N hand-written checks that each carried a message, list which messages become dead (an unused-symbol check finds them) and decide per message before pushing.

evidence: Duplicate of F2 on the same line: the adapter dropped `usage`, and the existing test bypassed `withWorkspaceSchema`. Fixed by the same `adaptLeaf` change.
guidance_note: Test a leaf through the registered production path, not through the inner constructor the wrapper calls.

evidence: Duplicate of F4: the same comment describes the deleted arity check. Rewritten in a1dc06b.
guidance_note: When deleting a check, rewrite every comment that names it in the same hunk.

evidence: The agent wired three leaves and declined lifeboat and snapshots with a defensible reason (the derived sentence still names the flag). It claimed `workflowsOverviewLeaf` was fixed after testing `lit workflows a b c`, which routes to the family rather than the leaf, and F12 shows that leaf was never wired.
guidance_note: Before reporting a leaf fixed, confirm the probe actually reaches that leaf (here `--` was needed), not just that the output matched.

evidence: The `[LAW:no-silent-failure]` justification was left above `config.Load` after its check was deleted; the agent moved it to the leaf declaration.
guidance_note: When deleting a check, rewrite every comment that names it in the same hunk.

evidence: The hunk shows `showLeaf` still holding 'usage: lit show <id> [--field ...]' only for the too-few branch; the agent hoisted or wired 11 leaves and declined `orphanedLeaf`, which still names `--assignee`, and listed it in the changelog.
guidance_note: When centralizing a check, diff every invocation path's refusal text against the base binary before the first push, not after reviewers enumerate them.

evidence: The agent verified on the binary that `lit upgrade --to --help` sets `--to` to '--help', which disproves the comment's 'refusal that shape already earned'. The packet does not show whether this comment predates review, so no cause is assigned.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that asserts what a library does with an input, run the input against the library.

evidence: The agent admits its F8 claim that `workflowsOverviewLeaf` carried `workflowsUsage` was checked with `lit workflows a b c`, which never reached the leaf; the `usage:` field was never added.
guidance_note: Verify a per-leaf fix with a probe proven to reach that leaf, or by reading the declaration, not by matching output.

evidence: The agent reproduced it: `lit label add --by -- <id> <label>` applied the label with `--by="--"`. The packet does not show whether the `--` branch predates review, so no cause is assigned. The fix covered only the exact-ceiling shape, and F14, F16, and F17 followed.
guidance_note: When fixing an argv-splitting bug, test the shape at ceiling, ceiling+1, and ceiling-1 tokens after the trigger, not just the reported one.

evidence: The F13 fix withheld only `--`, so an overflow token landed next to the dangling flag; the agent reproduced `--by="stray"` and a comment write. It returned early instead of routing every token, and F19's hunk shows that early return then dropped tokens (`lit init --prefix --prefix -- stray`).
guidance_note: When a fix withholds one token from a stream, enumerate what then becomes adjacent to the dangling consumer and test the overflow shape.

evidence: `importTreeLeaf` got `usage: importUsage` in a1dc06b (the F10 fix), yet the rewritten changelog listed `lit import` among the derived-sentence examples; the agent conceded it had filed it under the wrong mechanism.
guidance_note: When a changelog lists examples of a mechanism, check each member's code path, since each example is a separate claim.

evidence: Same overflow defect as F14 in the F13 fix; the reviewer's 'refuse outright' option matches the agent's early return in 28c80e1.
guidance_note: Test the reported shape plus one extra trailing token whenever a fix changes how argv tokens are routed.

evidence: The reviewer correctly showed the 'stays behind the terminator' comment is false when `--` was withheld; the agent used an early return rather than re-emitting `--`.
guidance_note: When a fix makes one branch skip emitting a token, re-read every comment in that loop that assumes the token was emitted.

evidence: The F1 fix replaced an accurate generic message with one naming `--eject=LIST`, which the agent confirmed is shown for `lit quickstart work --refresh`. The reviewer's `--force` path is wrong, because the `*force && !ejectChanged` guard returns first.
guidance_note: When rewording a refusal reached by several conditions, list each condition that reaches it and check that the new text is true for each.

evidence: The early-return fix for F14 dropped tokens, so splitArgs was rewritten to pair unconditionally, and `--` became a flag value again. The agent showed master refused `lit label add --by -- <id> mylabel` at exit 2 while the branch applied it, and `TestSplitArgsAgreesWithPflagAboutValues` pinned the bug.
guidance_note: When rewriting a parser for the third time, keep the earlier rounds' repro commands as permanent regression tests so a rewrite cannot quietly reopen one.

evidence: Duplicate of F19; the reviewer proposed withholding `--` so pflag errors, and the agent refused with its own message naming `--by=--`, verified at exit 2.
guidance_note: Keep earlier rounds' repro commands as regression tests across parser rewrites.

evidence: The agent measured that `lit sync reconcile zzz-a ...` routes to subcommand lookup, so adding it to `bareFormsThatAreLeaves` would fail. The real gap was the family branch the F3 fix added, which asserted only the command's own name and so was satisfied by any refusal; it now requires a registry-listed child name.
guidance_note: When adding a weaker assertion branch to a test, mutate the subject to a wrong-but-erroring output and confirm the branch goes red.

evidence: This is the third report of the F19 defect; the reviewer's 'refuse loudly' matches 19444cd, and the agent notes the test had pinned `--body` taking '--' as correct.
guidance_note: A test that asserts parity with a library must not pin a shape an earlier round proved was a bug.

narrative: Centralizing the stray-positional refusal was right, but splitArgs' handling of `--` went through three fixes. F13's guard covered only the exact-ceiling case, the early return for F14/F16/F17 dropped tokens, and the rewrite to 'model pflag exactly' let `--` become a flag value again, turning a master refusal into a write (F19/F20/F22). Smaller chains came from a reworded refusal that was false for --refresh (F18), a leaf claimed fixed through a probe that never reached it (F12), a vacuous test branch added for bare forms (F21), and a changelog example filed under the wrong mechanism (F15). Every finding from round 2 on was fix-caused, and the PR hit the five-round cap, so its head was never reviewed.
guidance_observations: The `--`/value-flag fixes each pinned only the reported shape, so a matrix test over ceiling-1, ceiling, and ceiling+1 trailing tokens on the first fix would have collapsed three rounds.

The agent verified with probes that did not reach the code under test (F8, F12) and with a parity test that pinned a known bug (F22); evidence-by-binary is only as good as proof that the probe exercises the target.
Reworded user-facing messages and changelog examples, each written while fixing something else, produced their own findings in later rounds.

evidence: The reviewer itself says the baseline 'was already drifted by roughly 85-100 lines before this PR', and the agent shows `model.go:369-371` at origin/master was already off by about 88 lines. The PR only kept the stale citations stable; the corpus-wide recompute was deferred to ticket links-docs-gwlf, a scoped decline rather than an acceptance despite the 'accept' hint.
guidance_note: When a PR mechanically shifts citations in a corpus known to be stale, say so in the PR body up front, with the tracking ticket, so the reviewer does not raise it per line.

evidence: Same pre-existing drift as F1: the diff shifts `631-712` to `638-719`, preserving an already-wrong pointer; the agent declined, citing links-docs-gwlf.
guidance_note: When a PR mechanically shifts citations in a corpus known to be stale, say so in the PR body up front, with the tracking ticket.

evidence: The diff shifts `lifecycle.go:111-121` to `154-164`, preserving pre-existing drift away from `DefaultOpen`; the agent used the same scoped decline.
guidance_note: When a PR mechanically shifts citations in a corpus known to be stale, say so in the PR body up front, with the tracking ticket.

evidence: `369-371` became `376-378`, both missing `IsContainer`; the agent's render at origin/master shows the original was already wrong by about 88 lines.
guidance_note: When a PR mechanically shifts citations in a corpus known to be stale, say so in the PR body up front, with the tracking ticket.

evidence: store.go:1543 still interpolated `w.action` while 1441 moved to `.Verb()`. internal/store first appears in round 1's scope, so this was work the agent added mid-review, not a fix for a finding; the agent says 'the second site of the class my own sweep missed'.
guidance_note: When introducing a Name/Verb split, find interpolation sites by type (go/types or AST over ActionName-typed expressions), not by grepping the method name at use sites.

evidence: The agent says `store.go:1737-1740` already named the wrong file on origin/master, so the branch shifted a number in an already-wrong citation; the six other examples are the same pre-existing class, deferred to links-docs-gwlf.

The agent again declined the corpus recompute but found and fixed four citations the branch did falsify (`workflow_events.go` 106 to 110), which slipped through because its resolver walked to a unique line before the insertion and skipped the comma-tail form. The reviewer's 'drop the numbers' alternative was not addressed.
guidance_note: Validate a citation relocator with a span immediately after an insertion and with every citation spelling before trusting its 'byte-identical' certificate.

evidence: The gate added in 54cf95c for F5 scanned with `fmt\.(?:Errorf|Sprintf)\([^\n]*`, so wrapped calls and Fprintf went unseen. The agent first adopted the reviewer's balanced-paren cure, which failed open on a `)` inside a literal (F11), and only then moved to go/parser.
guidance_note: Build a source-scanning gate on the language's parser from the start and mutation-test it against wrapped, nested, and literal-paren shapes before claiming coverage.

evidence: `actionNameBearers = {"w.action", "e.Action"}` was a literal list checked only by count, so a receiver rename empties the gate; the round-3 header shows the bearers now derived from declarations.
guidance_note: A completeness tripwire must check the identity of what it guards, not a count beside a hand-kept list.

evidence: The rewritten header's 'what it does not cover' omitted the concatenation site its own text cites (`"bulk " + action.Name().Verb()`); the agent added `TestBulkUsageNamesTheTypedVerb` and named the blind spot, one of the reviewer's two options.
guidance_note: When a gate's header lists its blind spots, check each historical miss it cites against the gate and list any the gate cannot see.

evidence: The balanced-paren matcher written for F8 counted parens inside string literals and silently skipped unbalanced calls; the agent confirmed `fmt.Sprintf("cannot :) %s", e.Action)` passed and replaced the matcher with go/parser.
guidance_note: Never accept a reviewer's text-matching cure for a code-structure question; reach for the parser.

narrative: The doc-citation findings (F1-F4, F6, F7) were pre-existing drift that the PR kept stable, and the agent declined a corpus recompute with a ticket, which was correct; F7 did surface four citations the branch really broke. F5 was a missed site in work added mid-review. Its fix introduced a regex gate that failed open three times (single-line, hardcoded bearers, paren-in-literal), each costing a round, until it was rebuilt on go/parser. The PR hit the five-round cap.
guidance_observations: A lint-style gate written as regex over Go source produced three consecutive fix-caused findings; parsing from the start would have saved rounds 3 and 4.
Six findings re-raised the same pre-existing citation drift because the PR did not state up front that it preserved, rather than corrected, known-stale citations.
Identical multi-paragraph replies posted on four threads at once made it hard to tell which specific change answered which finding.
